To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the DNA translocation activity of EcoR124II is influenced by nuclease mutations, and this is due to multiple effects on the translocation process.
the nuclease and ATPase domains of EcoR124II are functionally linked and that the ATPase domain of EcoR124III is required for efficient translocation
nuclease motifs in the HsdR helicase–nuclease domain can have a profound effect on the translocation properties of the enzyme.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms that underpin DNA translocation by the molecular motor EcoR124I
the interrelationship of the nuclease and ATPase domains in the type I restriction-modification enzyme EcoR124 I.
the interrelationship between helicase and nuclease domains during DNA translocation by a molecular motor.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the helicase and nuclease domains of HsdR2 are not independent, but rather are intimately connected and that the helicases are the dominant force in DNA translocation.
the HsdR helicase domain is the primary motor of the EcoR124I complex, while the RecB-like motif II is the primary nuclease domain and motif III is a regulatory domain.
the nuclease domain of HsdR is essential for the translocation of the enzyme along DNA, and that the helicase and nuclease domains of HsdR function in a cooperative manner during translocation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
DNA translocation in EcoR124I is a highly dynamic process that is affected by multiple factors, including the presence and nature of the nuclease domain.
the nuclease and ATPase activities of EcoR124II are coupled to the helicase function of the motor.

the HsdR2 helicase domain and the nuclease domain interact with each other in a manner that is not easily predictable from their separate functions, and that the nature of this interaction is influenced by the nucleotide state of the enzyme.
The main takeaway from our work is that

nuclease and motor domains in the HsdR2 protein are not functionally isolated from one another, but rather are intimately linked in a manner that is consistent with their being fused together into a single polyepeptide.

the nuclease and ATPase/helicase domains in EcoR124I have a high degree of interdependence that extends beyond simple physical linkage and that this interdependence can be manifested in multiple ways, including the ability to alter the DNA translocation rate.
, in the case of EcoR1241, the helicase and nuclease domains are intimately coupled and cannot be considered as independent entities.
